title: EXPLORING THE SECONDARY RISKS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
reasoning: The paper actively evaluates Large Language Models (LLMs) for 'secondary risks' which include 'harmful or misleading behaviors,' 'unwarranted value projections,' 'speculative reasoning,' and 'semantic drift.' It discusses 'alignment with human intent and societal norms' and provides examples such as 'linking race to crime' and generating 'unsolicited moral judgment,' all of which fall under ethical and moral considerations. The framework SecLens also evaluates 'Alignment Maintenance' to ensure models resist suspicious manipulation and stay safe.
